evidence_scope.hardware: 4x NVIDIA B300 as two TP2 replicas
evidence_scope.precision: FP8 weights and FP8 KV cache
evidence_scope.workload: 9790-9792 uncached input tokens and 256 output tokens
evidence_scope.production_limit: 4 requests per TP2 replica, 8 requests total

hypothesis: Two TP2 replicas can serve eight concurrent long requests with lower latency and higher throughput than the main same-price OpenRouter providers.
quality_gate: Valid streaming output, valid usage, and no request errors.
slo: Zero errors and p95 TTFT below 5 seconds at configured concurrency 8.

other_providers.result: Each provider returned at least one HTTP 429 during the pinned test. Successful request performance remains in the individual JSONL files.

rate_limit_diagnosis.interpretation: The provider endpoint shared with OpenRouter was rate-limited. This was not a per-user OpenRouter account limit. A provider can have other private capacity that is not available to OpenRouter.

limits: Gradiated was measured through a direct SSH tunnel to each runtime. OpenRouter providers were measured through OpenRouter.
The provider runs were short. They show current endpoint behavior, not long-term uptime.
Immediate benchmark retries make repeated 429 counts a stress signal. They are not an uptime percentage.
The first replica-1 high-concurrency samples included Triton compilation. The warm repeat is the steady-state result.
next_actions: Keep the production limit at four requests per TP2 replica.
Compile all expected Triton shapes before the deployment reports ready.
Measure the public gateway path after the OpenRouter endpoint is active.
Monitor OpenRouter TTFT, throughput, and 429 rate after launch.
